content.text: I have fedora running and test data installed. Now on the fun bits...
Running testing notes
it would be nice for instructions to specify how to tell the importer to read the resource uris from the manifest . had to look at the code to figure this out. (i.e the value to use for -R)
Is .binary (defined as a constant in
https://github.com/fcrepo4-labs/fcrepo-import-export/blob/master/src/main/java/org/fcrepo/importexport/common/FcrepoConstants.java#L35)

the only supported extension type for non rdf resources? Is this a Fedora restriction? Is it configurable per Fedora instance?  ( irc response from escowles: we didn't really have any use cases for customizable extensions, but you can add one to the import-export design wiki page)
I am not sure I fully understand this comment:
it would be nice for instructions to specify how to tell the importer to read the resource uris from the manifest . had to look at the code to figure this out. (i.e the value to use for -R)
Can you elaborate?

Sorry, yes I mean if you are importing a resource which doesn't exist in the repository already and you want it to find and import the resources that are in the bag.  In that case it seems you need to specify the host of the repo as the value of the  -R parameter.  (I haven't actually succeeded in getting anything to import yet though so I'm not sure if that's right...)
Hmm, you may have already done this, but the options and there descriptions can be found by executing the following:
java -jar fcrepo-import-export-0.1.0.jar --help
If you can describe where you are running into issues in the IRC channel, I suspect someone will be able to help.

I think the problem I'm having with importing is due to a misconception on my part about how much the import tool could do. Looking at the code, I guess data I import must explicitly adhere to the LDP container model. No mapping for free it seems

That's not super surprising and I can work on how to do the mapping, but I think in general, the import/export documentation could probably be improved to be more verbose about what it expects the contents of a directory to be imported to look like, and what model the resources needed to adhere to.  Or at least some pointers to existing documentation on that topic.
: I agree that some we need some introductory text to lay out the scope more clearly.  How does this sound:
The Fedora 4 Import/Export Utility is designed to export data from, and import data to, Fedora 4 for uses such as:
Migrating or synchronizing data from one repository to another
Exporting data for backup or preservation
Note
: The Import/Export Utility does not perform any data mapping or transformation — it can be used to import new data into Fedora, but the data would need to conform to Fedora's requirements.
That sounds good. Maybe with a link to where one can find the description of "Fedora's requirements"?
: Here is a new documentation ticket:
https://jira.duraspace.org/browse/FCREPO-2455

My recommendation is that we close this item. Based upon what I've learned through testing, I think packages produced by Perseids with the intent of being imported into Fedora should probably not follow the RO model but instead be explicitly represented via the LDP containment model. We will try with Perseids support both options, but the cost/benefit of trying to do them in one package doesn't seem to be there.
Thanks for your input,
This task is to verify the BagIt profile created in:
https://jira.duraspace.org/browse/FCREPO-2306
Potentially useful instructions:
Download the utility:
https://github.com/fcrepo4-labs/fcrepo-import-export/releases
Have a running Fedora
If you do not have a Fedora to test with, you may want to start up the "one-click run":
https://wiki.duraspace.org/display/FEDORA4x/Quick+Start#QuickStart-One-ClickRun
Have data in your Fedora
If you do not have data in your Fedora, you will likely want to load some of your own or one of the existing example datasets:
https://github.com/fcrepo4-labs/fcrepo-sample-dataset/tree/master/additional_datasets

Although there are minimal instructions in the readme linked above, if you run into issues loading any of these datasets, I would be happy to help... the possibility of issues arising is not inconceivable.
Export your data as Bagit bags
Here are some minimal instructions:
https://github.com/fcrepo4-labs/fcrepo-import-export/blob/master/README.md#running-the-importexport-utility-with-a-bagit-support
To export APTrust-style bags, use the ''--bag-profile aptrust" argument when running the utility.
The question to be answered is: Are the APTrust-style bags that the utility creates actually compliant with the APTrust expectations/requirements?
